pages.text: The Prior Claimant ruled before the current age and will rule again after it. This is not prophecy — it is a description of what ruling means to the Prior Claimant, which is different from what ruling means to those who have succeeded it. The Prior Claimant does not govern. The Prior Claimant holds. A thing that hath been held by the Prior Claimant retains the shape of that holding long after the holding has ended. The barrows are the most obvious example. The barrows were always the most obvious example. That they were obvious did not help.

The creatures that emerge from the barrows are not the dead returning. They are the holding, continuing. The Prior Claimant hath not released them. The Prior Claimant hath never released anything. This is what Prior means — not prior in time, though that too, but prior in claim. The claim was made before anything else was owned, and it hath not been relinquished.

When thou art in a barrow, thou art in the Prior Claimant's hand. The Prior Claimant is not home. The hand hath not opened.
